newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel agrees to Jewish settlement "pause" - PLO.
newsitem.headline: Israel agrees to Jewish settlement "pause" - PLO.

text.p: PLO officials said Israel had agreed in principle to an unspecified "pause" in Jewish settlement building, clearing the way for a meeting with Israeli negotiators in Cairo on Sunday.

"The change in the Israeli government's position on this issue in particular and its acceptance in principle of a 'pause' in settlement activities made it possible to hold this meeting at the experts level," Marwan Kanafani, spokesman to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, told Reuters from Cairo.
The meeting was due to begin at 1400 GMT in Cairo.

But Israeli officials insisted Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing government remained committed to building settlements on land occupied in 1967 in the West Bank, including in Arab East Jerusalem, as well as in the Gaza Strip.
"Israel doesn't agree to stop or to freeze the settlements and the meeting in Cairo is without preconditions," Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak told Reuters. "It's not correct."
Talks with the PLO have been stuck since Israel broke ground three months ago for the Har Homa settlement on an East Jerusalem hill which Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim.

PLO officials said Egyptian and Israeli officials had informed the PLO of the change in the Israeli position on settlement activities. But they said they were sceptical of making progress, suspecting Israel was playing with words.
The precise meaning of a "pause" was vague, they said.
Netanyahu's confidant, the Israeli mayor of Jerusalem Ehud Olmert, told Israeli army radio he drew a distinction between expansion of existing settlements and construction of new ones.
Palestinians said there were no distinctions.
Egypt has intensified its peacemaking role in the three-month-old crisis since a summit between President Hosni Mubarak and Netanyahu last month.

Diplomatic sources said Egypt was pushing a five-point plan which included a freeze on any change in the status of Jerusalem and a ban on Jewish settlement building in the West Bank for "a sufficient period".
In return the Palestinians would give a firm commitment to address Israel's security demands, the sources added.
Construction at the Har Homa site continued on Sunday. An Israeli construction chief, Eli Ezra, said he had about 30 Jews, Romanians and Jerusalem Arabs working at the site.
Asked by army radio if Arabs were helping to build the project of 6,500 housing units, he said: "You could say so."
More than 130,000 Jews live in settlements scattered throughout the West Bank and Gaza Strip, areas captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war and home to more than two million Palestinians.
